title: The Pareto Frontier of Randomized Learning-Augmented Online Bidding
claim: Our upper bound matches the lower bound for large robustness, closing the gap that earlier strategies left open.
layout: 2 side-by-side line plots, zoomed left (narrow range) and wide right
description: Two side-by-side line plots share the same y-axis, consistency, which runs from 1 to e. The x-axis is robustness. The left panel is a zoomed view of robustness from e to 2/ln(2), about 2.885. The right panel covers robustness from e to 6. Each panel has several curves in different colors and line styles. A dashed orange curve is the highest. A dashed purple curve drops steeply near x = e. A dotted blue curve and a gray step-like curve sit close together in the middle. A dotted green curve is the lowest and acts as the lower bound. In the right panel, a thick solid black curve runs just above the green curve and meets it as robustness grows. This shows the upper and lower bounds converging. There is no legend, so the caption identifies the curves. The eye goes first to the steep curves near the top left and then follows them down to where they converge.
caption: Consistency--robustness tradeoff for various bidding strategies and different ranges of the robustness $R$. The dashed orange curve corresponds to the bidding sequence from [ref], while the dotted green curve corresponds to the lower bound given in [ref]. UB and LB denote upper and lower bounds, respectively.
abstract: Online bidding is a classical problem in online decision-making, with applications in resource allocation, hierarchical clustering, and the analysis of approximation algorithms. We study its randomized learning-augmented variant, where an online algorithm generates a sequence of random bids while leveraging predictions from an oracle. We provide analytical upper and lower bounds on the optimal consistency $C$ as a function of the robustness $R$, which match when $R \geq 2.885$, effectively closing the gap left by previous work. The key technical ingredient is the notion of a bidding function, a novel abstraction that provides a unified framework for the design and analysis of randomized bidding strategies. We complement our theoretical results with an experimental application of randomized bidding to the incremental median problem, demonstrating the applicability of our algorithm in practical clustering settings.
